# Introduction

The objective of this notebook is to perform a basic quality control of the mapping performed with [Cellranger](https://support.10xgenomics.com/single-cell-multiome-atac-gex/software/pipelines/latest/what-is-cell-ranger-arc). Cell Ranger ARC analyzes data generated by the Chromium Single Cell Multiome ATAC + Gene Expression. Should note here, we will talk about features that can refer to a gene (declared from the hg38 reference transcriptome) or a peak (determined by the Peak Calling algorithm provided by Cell Ranger). 

Parts of this report have been recycled from [TONSIL project](https://github.com/Single-Cell-Genomics-Group-CNAG-CRG/tonsil_atlas/tree/preprint_atac)

Before reading the report, let's clarify some terms. 

Fragment and read in ATAC: Each fragment is created by two separate transposition events, which create the two ends of the observed fragment. Each unique fragment may generate multiple duplicate reads in the sequencing. 

Barcode: The 10X barcoded gel beads consist of a pool barcodes which are used to separately index each cell's transcriptome. So barcoe and cell are sometimes used interchangeably

# Summary Metrics 

## Metrics table

```{r}
qc_samples %>% 
  DT::datatable(fillContainer = T) 
```
From table, some of the informative metrics are the following (more info about them [here](https://assets.ctfassets.net/an68im79xiti/6uFMwMQwMySzluyIeBZhMl/e5acb853870c59d3f3fc826428cb6d3c/CG000368_TechnicalNote_InterpretingARCWebSummaryFilesforMultiomeATAC_GEX_RevA.pdf)):

  * _Median number of genes_ should be between 2000~2500.
  * _Estimated number of cells_ should be similar to the number of nuclei used 
  * _Median high-quality fragments per cell_ this may vary according to sequencing depth (but at least > 100)
  * _Feature linkage genes_ is expected to be above 100 000. This metric means the total number of gene-peak and peak-peak linkages detected.


Other ATAC specific metrics might indicate excessive transposition background (due to a population 
of cells with un-compacted DNA such as granulocytes or dying cells) or also indicate an 
unexpected behaviour of the peak calling algorithm.

  * _Fragments in peaks_ expected values > 25%
  * _Fraction of transposition events within peaks_ expected values > 25%. That is the fraction of transposition events that are associated with cell-containing partitions and fall within peaks
  * _TSS enrichment_ ideally > 5. TSS regions (known to be open) are expected to have lots of  cut  sites  from  accessible  fragments. A part from a transposition issue, a low value might also indicate poor sample preparation or poor sample quality. 
      
## Compare estimated number of cells between samples

```{r}
barplot_data(melt(qc_samples[, c("patient","Estimated number of cells")])) + coord_flip()
```

```{r}
print(paste("Total number of estimated cells in all samples:", sum(qc_samples$"Estimated number of cells")))
```

## Plots of feature linkages

Feature linkages are defined as pairs of genomic features, such as peaks and genes, that have significant correlation in signals across cells. Concretely, the feature linkage is calculated taking into account genes with its proximal peaks and between pairs of proximal peaks across the genome. A low number of feature links detected may be caused by a low number of nuclei recovered, low sequencing  depth, poor peak calling, or a sample that is relatively homogeneous. More information about feature linkages [here](https://support.10xgenomics.com/single-cell-multiome-atac-gex/software/pipelines/latest/algorithms/feature-linkage)

```{r}
barplot_data(melt(qc_samples[,c("patient",
                                "Linked genes",
                                "Linked peaks")]))
```

```{r}
linkage_melt <- melt(qc_samples[,c("patient",
                                   "Feature linkages detected")])
barplot_data(multiome_melted = linkage_melt)
```

## Cross sensitivity plot from Cell Ranger

Each dot is a barcode. In orange are cells whereas in blue there are the non-cell barcodes. 
x-axis reflects the number of ATAC transposition events in peaks associated with that barcode, while the position on the y-axis corresponds to the number of gene expression UMI counts.

Create a list of Seurat objects (1 per sample)
```{r fig.height = 8, fig.width = 14, out.width = "100%"}

list_objects <- lapply(qc_samples$gem_id, function(id) {
  #print(id)
  obj <- create_object(id)
  obj <- add_bc_info(id, obj)
})

list_objects <- setNames(list_objects, qc_samples$patient)

list_plots <- lapply(seq_along(list_objects), function(i) {
  # parameters
  id <- names(list_objects[i])
  obj <- list_objects[[i]]
  
  # orientative cutoffs
  x_atac_cutoff <- min(obj@meta.data[obj@meta.data$is_cell == 1, "nCount_ATAC"])+10
  y_rna_cutoff <- min(obj@meta.data[obj@meta.data$is_cell == 1, "nCount_RNA"])+4
  
  # plot
  plot_cross_sense(obj, id, x_atac_cutoff, y_rna_cutoff)
})

cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = list_plots,
                   ncol=2,
                   align = "hv",
                   axis = "trbl")
```

Comments on plot: Ideally, the orange and blue cloud of points should **not** overlap and separate a bit so that the centroid of the orange cloud (barcodes considered cells) should be on the top right corner. 

# ATAC Checks

## Sequencing

### Sequenced read pairs

The following plot shows the number of sequencing read pairs of each multiome ATAC library. In this case each sample comes from 1 donor and 1 library was performed. According to the documentation, the optimal number of read pairs are 25,000 per cell here shown with a dashed line. 

```{r}
qc_samples$"ATAC Mean raw read pairs per cell" <- round(qc_samples$"ATAC Mean raw read pairs per cell",2)
ggbarplot(qc_samples,
  x = "patient",
  y = "ATAC Mean raw read pairs per cell",
  label = TRUE,
  fill = "gray70",
  ggtheme = theme_pubr(x.text.angle = 45,legend = "none")) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept  = 25000, linetype='dotted', col = 'black')
```
The following plot shows the quality of the sequenced read pairs of each ATAC library. A high-quality read-pair is one with mapping quality > 30. These means reads with a Q-score ≥ 30. Q-score is calculated in the following way:
$$Q = -10\log10(p)$$
where *p* is the probability of the base being wrongly called. Thus, bases with a high Q-score are reliable.

```{r}
multiome_melted <- melt(qc_samples[,c("patient", "ATAC Q30 bases in barcode",
"ATAC Q30 bases in read 1",        
"ATAC Q30 bases in read 2")])
          
ggplot(multiome_melted, aes(variable, value)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = NA, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, height = 0) +
  geom_text_repel(data = multiome_melted, aes(label = patient, fill = "black")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
      axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"))
```
As long as all of these measurements are above 80% there are no concerns regarding read quality.

### Valid Barcodes

Fraction of read pairs with barcodes that match the whitelist after error correction. The barcode whitelist represents all known barcode sequences that have been included in the assay kit and are available during library preparation. Therefore, low valid barcodes may indicate a problem in the library preparation. Good quality library value should be above or around 85%. 

```{r}
ggbarplot(qc_samples,
  x = "patient",
  y =  "ATAC Valid barcodes",
  label = TRUE,
  fill = "gray70",
  ggtheme = theme_pubr(x.text.angle = 45,legend = "none")) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept  = 0.85, linetype='dotted', col = 'black')
```

### Percent of duplicates

We should expect an overall positive correlation between the duplicated data and the library size and sequencing depth.

```{r}
correlation_plot(qc_samples,"ATAC Percent duplicates","ATAC Sequenced read pairs")
```


```{r}
correlation_plot(qc_samples,"ATAC Percent duplicates","ATAC Number of peaks")
```

## Cells 

### Checking the quality of fragments in/per cell

Definition of high quality fragment: High quality fragments are defined as read pairs with a valid barcode that map to the nuclear genome with mapq > 30, are not chimeric and not duplicate. 

 * _Mean raw read pairs per cell_ : Total number of read pairs divided by the number of barcodes. This is a way to measure sequencing depth of the ATAC assay. 10x suggested depth is of 25,000 read pairs per cell. Values should be at least > 5000.
 * _Median high quality fragments per cell_: A lower than expected value may indicate low sequencing depth or low library complexity (at least >100)
 * _Fraction of high quality fragments in cell_: Fraction of high quality fragments with a valid barcode that are associated with cell-containing partitions (>40%)
 * _Fraction of transposition events in peaks in cells_: Transposition events are located at both ends of all high-quality fragments. This metric measures the percentage of such events that overlap with peaks. (>25%)
 
```{r}
qc_atac_read_pairs <- melt(qc_samples[,c("patient","ATAC Mean raw read pairs per cell", "ATAC Median high-quality fragments per cell")])
barplot_data(qc_atac_read_pairs)
```

```{r}
qc_atac_fraction <- melt(qc_samples[,c("patient", "ATAC Fraction of high-quality fragments in cells","ATAC Fraction of transposition events in peaks in cells")])
barplot_data(qc_atac_fraction)
```

## Targeting metrics

### Total number of peaks 

```{r}
ggbarplot(qc_samples, "patient", "ATAC Number of peaks",
  label = TRUE,
  fill = "gray70",
  ggtheme = theme_pubr(x.text.angle = 45,legend = "none"),
  position = position_dodge(0.9))
```

We should expect a positive correlation across samples (~donors in this case) between the median of high quality fragments per cell and the total number of peaks in that sample. 
```{r}
correlation_plot(qc_samples,"ATAC Number of peaks",
  "ATAC Median high-quality fragments per cell")
```

It's also interesting to check the Single Cell Peak Targeting Plot 

```{r fig.height = 8, fig.width = 14, out.width = "100%"}
list_plots <- lapply(seq_along(list_objects), function(i) {
  id <- names(list_objects[i])
  obj <- list_objects[[id]]
  plt <- ggplot(obj@meta.data, aes(x=atac_fragments, y=FRiP)) + 
      geom_point(aes(color=is_cell)) +
      scale_color_manual(breaks = c(0, 1), values=c("#56B4E9", "#E69F00")) +
      scale_x_log10() +
      ggtitle(glue::glue("Single Cell Peak Targeting Plot {id}")) + 
      theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
  return(plt)
})
  

cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = list_plots,
                   align = "hv",
                   axis = "trbl")
```

Comments on plot: Ideally, we expect a large number of fragments per barcode and a high percentage of fragments overlapping peaks (orange centroid in the upper right corner) for the cell barcodes. Whereas for the non-cell barcodes we should expect a small number of fragments per barcode and a low percentage of fragments overlapping peaks (blue cloud of points in the lower left corner). Accumulation of orange and blue dots tightly concentrated in the same location may indicate issues with cell calling or sample preparation. 

### Characterization of high quality fragments 

 * _Fraction of high-quality fragments overlapping peaks_: Fraction of high-quality fragments in cell barcodes that overlap called peaks.(>25%)
 * _Fraction of high-quality fragments overlapping TSS_: Fraction of high-quality fragments in cell barcodes that overlap transcription start sites (TSS). (expected between 40-50% in our experience)

```{r fig.height = 5, fig.width = 14, out.width = "100%"}

multiome_melted <- melt(qc_samples[,c("patient", "ATAC Fraction of high-quality fragments in cells",
"ATAC Fraction of high-quality fragments overlapping peaks", "ATAC Fraction of high-quality fragments overlapping TSS")])
                 
multiome_melted$value = round(multiome_melted$value,2)                   
ggbarplot(multiome_melted, "patient", "value",
  fill = "variable", color = "variable", palette = "Paired",
  label = TRUE,
  ggtheme = theme_pubr(x.text.angle = 45),
  position = position_dodge(0.9))
```

### Transcription Start Site (TSS)

It is expected to obtain a large enrichment around TSS (> 5% EV, red dashed line), as these regions are known to show a high degree of chromatin accessibility compared to the flanking regions.

```{r}
data_tss <- qc_samples[, c("patient", "ATAC TSS enrichment score")]
data_tss.melt <- melt(data_tss)
barplot_data(data_tss.melt) + geom_hline(yintercept = 5, linetype = 2, color = "red")
```

# GEx checks

## Sequencing

### Median genes per cell

This  metric  is  dependent  on  sample  type  complexity  and sequencing depth. But from our experience it should be between 2000~2500.
```{r}
median_genes_gg <- melt(qc_samples[,c("patient","GEX Median genes per cell")])
barplot_data(median_genes_gg)
```


### Sequenced read pairs

Total number of read pairs divided by the number of cell barcodes. This metric is a function of the number of cell and sequencing depth. 10x suggested depth is of 20,000 read pairs per cell
```{r}
#qc_samples$"GEX Mean raw reads per cell" <- round(qc_samples$"GEX Mean raw reads per cell", 2)
ggbarplot(qc_samples,
  x = "patient",
  y =  "GEX Mean raw reads per cell",
  label = TRUE,
  fill = "gray70",
  ggtheme = theme_pubr(x.text.angle = 45)) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept  = 20000, linetype='dotted', col = 'black')
```

Just like in the ATAC section, here we can also check the read quality.

```{r}
multiome_melted <- melt(qc_samples[,c("patient", "GEX Q30 bases in barcode",
"GEX Q30 bases in UMI", "GEX Q30 bases in read 2")])

ggplot(multiome_melted, aes(variable, value)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = NA, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, height = 0) +
  geom_text_repel(data = multiome_melted, aes(label = patient, fill = "black")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
      axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"))
```

### Valid barcodes

As explained in the ATAC section above, we can plot the read pairs with whitelist barcodes (>80%)

```{r}
ggbarplot(qc_samples,
  x = "patient",
  y =  "GEX Valid barcodes",
  label = TRUE,
  fill = "gray70",
  ggtheme = theme_pubr(x.text.angle = 45,legend = "none")) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept  = 0.85, linetype='dotted', col = 'black')
```

### Percent of duplicates

```{r}
correlation_plot(qc_samples,"GEX Percent duplicates","GEX Sequenced read pairs")
```

```{r}
correlation_plot(qc_samples,"GEX Percent duplicates","GEX Total genes detected")
```

## Mapping 

Secondly, we will assess the quality of cellranger’s mapping by comparing the percentage of reads mapping to the genome, intergenic regions, intronic and exonic regions across libraries. Reads mapping to intergenic regions suggest contamination of ambient DNA, while reads mapping to intronic regions may come from pre-mRNAs or mature splice isoforms that retain the introns.

The fraction of sequenced reads that map to a unique gene in the transcriptome is expected to be higher than the 50%

```{r}
qc_samples$"GEX Fraction of transcriptomic reads in cells" <- round(qc_samples$"GEX Fraction of transcriptomic reads in cells",2)
ggbarplot(qc_samples,
  x = "patient",
  y =  "GEX Fraction of transcriptomic reads in cells",
  fill = "gray70",
  label = TRUE,
  ggtheme = theme_pubr(x.text.angle = 45)) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept  = 0.50, linetype='dotted', col = 'black')
```

```{r}
multiome_melted <- melt(qc_samples[,c("patient", "GEX Reads mapped to genome",  
                                      "GEX Reads mapped confidently to genome")])
                
multiome_melted$value <- round(multiome_melted$value,2)                    
ggbarplot(multiome_melted, 
          x = "patient", 
          y = "value",
          fill = "variable", palette = "Paired",  label = TRUE,
  ggtheme = theme_pubr(x.text.angle = 45),
  position = position_dodge(0.9))
```

In the following plot, the fraction of sequenced reads that map to a unique gene in the transcriptome is expected to be higher than 50% (blue dashed line). However, the percentatge of reads mapped confidently to intergenic regions and reads mapped antisense to gene are expected to be lower than 30% (red dashed line).

```{r fig.height = 5, fig.width = 16, out.width = "100%"}
mapping_qc_vars <- c(
  "patient",
  "GEX Reads mapped confidently to intergenic regions",
  "GEX Reads mapped confidently to intronic regions",
  "GEX Reads mapped confidently to exonic regions",
  "GEX Reads mapped confidently to transcriptome",
  "GEX Reads mapped antisense to gene")

mapping_qc_gg.melt <- melt(qc_samples[,mapping_qc_vars])

mapping_qc_gg.melt$value <- round(mapping_qc_gg.melt$value,2)                    
ggbarplot(mapping_qc_gg.melt, 
          x = "patient", 
          y = "value",
          fill = "variable", palette = "Paired",  label = TRUE,
  ggtheme = theme_pubr(x.text.angle = 45),
  position = position_dodge(0.9))+
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.text=element_text(size=14)) +
  guides(fill = ggplot2::guide_legend(nrow = 2))+
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.3,0.5), col = c("red","blue"),  linetype='dotted')
```
